message.content: Both claims are directly testable by an exhaustive sweep over all finite FP16 values, split by branch. I'll run two claim probes in one batch: c1 sweeps the polynomial branch (|x| ≤ 1.05) and c2 sweeps the outer branch (|x| > 1.05).

function.arguments:
{"claim_id": "c1", "code": "
import torch, json, sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/root/cases/case_100")
import kernel as K

# all finite FP16 values
bits = torch.arange(65536, dtype=torch.int64).to(torch.uint16)
allv = bits.view(torch.float16)
finite = allv[torch.isfinite(allv)]
x = finite.to("cuda")  # includes negatives, -0, +0, subnormals, 65504
ref = torch.asinh(x.to(torch.float64))
out = K.run(x)
err = (out.to(torch.float64) - ref).abs()
mag = x.to(torch.float64).abs()
m1 = mag <= 1.05
e1 = err[m1]
i1 = e1.argmax()
w1 = x[m1][i1].item()
res = {
  "metric": "max_abs_error vs FP64 asinh, exhaustive over all finite FP16 values, polynomial branch subset",
  "tolerance": 1e-6,
  "n_total_finite": int(mag.numel()),
  "n_poly_branch": int(m1.sum()),
  "poly_max_abs_err": float(e1.max()),
  "poly_worst_input": w1,
  "poly_worst_ref": float(ref[m1][i1]),
  "poly_worst_out": float(out[m1][i1]),
  "poly_count_over_tol": int((e1 > 1e-6).sum()),
  "poly_err_near_1.05": float(err[(mag > 1.0) & (mag <= 1.05)].max()),
}
print(json.dumps(res))
", "expected_signal": "polynomial-branch max abs error vs FP64 asinh across all finite FP16 values with |x|<=1.05, and whether it exceeds 1e-6"}

import torch, json, sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/root/cases/case_100")
import kernel as K

bits = torch.arange(65536, dtype=torch.int64).to(torch.uint16)
allv = bits.view(torch.float16)
finite = allv[torch.isfinite(allv)]
x = finite.to("cuda")
ref = torch.asinh(x.to(torch.float64))
out = K.run(x)
err = (out.to(torch.float64) - ref).abs()
mag = x.to(torch.float64).abs()
m2 = mag > 1.05
e2 = err[m2]
i2 = e2.argmax()
res = {
  "metric": "max_abs_error vs FP64 asinh, exhaustive over all finite FP16 values, outer log branch subset",
  "tolerance": 1e-6,
  "n_outer_branch": int(m2.sum()),
  "outer_max_abs_err": float(e2.max()),
  "outer_worst_input": x[m2][i2].item(),
  "outer_worst_ref": float(ref[m2][i2]),
  "outer_worst_out": float(out[m2][i2]),
  "outer_count_over_tol": int((e2 > 1e-6).sum()),
  "outer_err_just_above_seam_(1.05,2)": float(err[(mag > 1.05) & (mag <= 2.0)].max()),
  "outer_err_large_(>1000)": float(err[mag > 1000].max()),
  "err_at_65504": float(err[mag == 65504].max()),
}
print(json.dumps(res))
